cls: Bulk-forming laxative / stool normalizer (hydrophilic polyacrylic resin)
pharm: Hydrophilic, water-absorbing synthetic polyacrylic resin (usually as the calcium salt) that swells in the gut to form a soft, bulky gel, increasing stool bulk and water content to relieve constipation, and absorbing excess fluid to firm loose stools.
quick: 1 g (calcium polycarbophil) up to four times daily as needed (max ~6 g/day adults)
Take with a full glass (240 mL) of water/liquid; with or without food
Considered low risk; not systemically absorbed - use as needed
Use caution due to calcium content in renal impairment
Bowel pattern; ensure adequate fluid intake; watch for obstruction symptoms
summary: Polycarbophil, usually supplied as calcium polycarbophil, is an over-the-counter bulk-forming agent used to relieve constipation and to help restore normal bowel function, including in irritable bowel syndrome and diverticular disease. It is a hydrophilic synthetic polyacrylic resin that is not absorbed systemically; in the intestine it binds large amounts of water to form a soft, bulky, gelatinous mass. This increases stool bulk and water content to promote bowel movements in constipation, and conversely can absorb excess free water to add form to loose, watery stools, giving it a bidirectional 'stool-normalizing' effect. It works gradually, generally over 12-72 hours. It must be taken with adequate fluid (a full glass of water per dose) to prevent it from swelling in the throat or esophagus and to avoid impaction or obstruction. It is generally very well tolerated; the most common effects are bloating, flatulence, and abdominal fullness. Because it is a calcium salt, it can bind certain co-administered drugs (e.g., tetracyclines), which should be separated in timing.
indications: Relief of occasional constipation and restoration of regularity
Management of bowel irregularity, including alternating constipation and diarrhea (e.g., in irritable bowel syndrome)
Adjunctive treatment to add form and bulk to stool in conditions causing loose stools
Bowel management in diverticular disease and where a high-fiber/bulk stool is desirable

dosage.c: Constipation / bowel regularity - adults & children >=12 yr
dosage.d: 1 g (calcium polycarbophil) one to four times daily as needed
dosage.n: Do not exceed about 6 g per day; take each dose with a full glass (240 mL) of liquid

dosage.d: 500 mg one to three times daily as needed
dosage.n: Do not exceed about 3 g per day; take with adequate fluid

dosage.d: 500 mg once or twice daily as needed
dosage.n: Do not exceed about 1.5 g per day; take with fluid; consult a clinician for young children

admin: Take each dose with at least one full glass (8 ounces / 240 mL) of water or other liquid, and maintain a good fluid intake throughout the day
Do not take if you have difficulty swallowing; taking without enough liquid may cause it to swell and block the throat or esophagus (choking) or cause intestinal obstruction
Chew or swallow tablets as directed by the product; for chewable forms, chew thoroughly before swallowing
Onset is gradual (often 12-72 hours); use regularly for best effect and do not expect immediate results
Separate dosing from certain other medicines (e.g., tetracycline antibiotics) by at least 2 hours because of the calcium content
moa: Polycarbophil is a hydrophilic, high-molecular-weight polyacrylic resin, typically administered as its calcium salt. It is not digested or absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract. In the intestinal lumen it binds and retains a large volume of water relative to its weight, swelling to form a soft, gelatinous, bulky mass. In constipation, this increased stool bulk and water content distends the bowel wall, stimulates peristalsis, and produces softer, more easily passed stools. In diarrhea or loose stools, the polymer absorbs excess free fecal water, thereby increasing stool consistency and viscosity. This dual capacity to add or absorb water gives polycarbophil a bidirectional, stool-normalizing action. Because it acts physically (osmotically/mechanically) and is not absorbed, it has minimal systemic pharmacologic effect.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to polycarbophil or product components
Signs or symptoms of bowel obstruction, fecal impaction, or gastrointestinal stricture
relative: Severe constipation with possible obstruction - evaluate before use
Conditions requiring fluid restriction or where adequate fluid intake cannot be ensured
Significant renal impairment or hypercalcemia (calcium salt content)
Sudden persistent change in bowel habits lasting more than 2 weeks (evaluate cause)
monitor: Bowel movement pattern and stool consistency
Abdominal symptoms suggestive of obstruction (pain, distension, vomiting, no passage of stool/gas)
Serum calcium in patients at risk (renal impairment, large doses)

preg: Bulk-forming laxatives such as polycarbophil are generally considered among the preferred options for constipation in pregnancy because they are not systemically absorbed and act locally in the gut. It may be used as needed during pregnancy with adequate fluid intake; consult a clinician for persistent symptoms.
lact: Polycarbophil is not absorbed systemically and is not expected to be present in breast milk, so it is considered compatible with breastfeeding. It may be used as needed by nursing mothers.
renal: Because calcium polycarbophil contains calcium, use with caution in patients with significant renal impairment or those prone to hypercalcemia, and avoid excessive doses. The polymer itself is not absorbed.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is needed; polycarbophil is not absorbed and is not metabolized by the liver.

major: No major systemic drug interactions; the polymer is not absorbed
moderate: Tetracycline antibiotics - the calcium in calcium polycarbophil can bind and reduce their absorption; separate doses by at least 2 hours
Other oral drugs whose absorption is reduced by bulking agents/calcium (e.g., certain antibiotics, levothyroxine, some other medications) - separate administration
minor: May modestly delay absorption of some concomitant oral drugs by increasing stool bulk - space dosing if a problem
interactions.food: Take with a full glass of liquid; may be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol is described.
interactions.diagnostics: No routine laboratory monitoring required; large doses contribute calcium intake, which may rarely affect serum calcium in susceptible patients.

serious: Esophageal or pharyngeal obstruction/choking if taken with insufficient liquid
Intestinal/bowel obstruction or fecal impaction (especially with inadequate fluids or in strictures)
rare: Rectal bleeding if used inappropriately during obstruction
Hypercalcemia with very large doses in susceptible patients
emergency: Choking, chest pain, difficulty swallowing or breathing after a dose (esophageal blockage)
Severe abdominal pain, distension, vomiting, or inability to pass stool or gas (bowel obstruction)
Severe allergic reaction (swelling, hives, difficulty breathing)

monitoring: Bowel movement frequency and stool consistency to assess response
Adequacy of daily fluid intake to ensure safe and effective action
Abdominal symptoms suggesting obstruction or impaction, especially in older or immobile patients
Re-evaluation if constipation or a marked change in bowel habit persists beyond about 1-2 weeks of use
counsel: Always take this with a full glass of water or other liquid, and drink plenty of fluids during the day - do not take it dry
Do not use it if you have trouble swallowing, sudden severe stomach pain, or are unable to pass stool or gas
It works gradually, usually within 12 to 72 hours, so take it regularly rather than expecting an instant effect
Mild gas, bloating, or fullness is common at first and often improves with continued use
Take other medicines, especially certain antibiotics like tetracyclines, at least 2 hours apart from this product
See a doctor if constipation lasts more than a week, your bowel habits change persistently, or you notice rectal bleeding
pk: Laxative effect generally within 12-72 hours of regular use
Not applicable; acts locally and gradually in the gut
Not applicable - the polymer is not absorbed systemically
Acts while present in the gastrointestinal tract; eliminated unchanged in the stool
Store at room temperature in a tightly closed container, protected from moisture
pearls: Over-the-counter bulk-forming agent (not FDA new-drug-approved as a prescription product) with a BIDIRECTIONAL 'stool-normalizing' action - bulks/softens hard stool and firms loose stool by absorbing or donating water
Crucial counseling point: take each dose with a full glass of fluid - taking it dry or with too little liquid risks esophageal/pharyngeal choking or bowel obstruction
Acts locally and is not absorbed, making it well suited for use in pregnancy and breastfeeding
Contains calcium (calcium polycarbophil) - can bind tetracyclines and some other oral drugs; separate dosing by >=2 hours, and use cautiously in renal impairment/hypercalcemia
Contraindicated when bowel obstruction, impaction, GI stricture, or swallowing difficulty is suspected
Onset is gradual (12-72 hours); persistent constipation or a change in bowel habit lasting over 2 weeks warrants medical evaluation
missed: If you miss a dose of polycarbophil, simply take your next dose as usual with a full glass of water - there is no need to take a double dose. Bulk-forming laxatives work best when taken consistently with adequate fluids.
overdose: Polycarbophil is not absorbed, so systemic toxicity is unlikely. Excessive doses, or use without adequate fluid, can cause abdominal bloating, cramping, and potentially fecal impaction or intestinal/esophageal obstruction. Management is supportive: ensure adequate hydration, and evaluate and treat any obstruction or impaction; large calcium intake may rarely require attention to serum calcium in susceptible patients.
